about: Timeline path 1 of 3, 'Binary' (docs/research/2026-10-01-timeline-brainstorm.md): the lines read as bits, Fu Xi to today. Opens on all three paths (series/explainers/timeline-paths.json) and flies down this one. Draft 2, Sol's rewrite of pages and caption (docs/research/2026-10-04-codex-timeline-binary-correspondence.md); page 1 keeps Answering's opener so the three paths open alike. Draft 1, from Sol's checked table (docs/research/2026-10-01-codex-timeline-paths.md): structure, not lineage; Fu Xi as legend; Shao Yong's order 'can be read as' binary; Bouvet sends 1701, Leibniz receives 1703 and had binary since 1679; Turing's machine is imagined; Shannon's bit; the C64's 64 is memory.
style: The header reads '8-BIT ORACLE // READY FOR INQUIRY' throughout (brand.header). Each query clears the screen like a filmbook page. The query is typed after '>' (dim green); the answer types out below it (bright green, 48 px); the part of the readout the answer is about is drawn beside it, alone. Chapter pages: a single word, centred, held 2 s. Own names only, never MU/TH/UR or INTERFACE 2037.

music.why: provisional, as on Answering: a track per path to choose

caption: The I-Ching's 64 line patterns fit in six bits. Reading them takes more: 8bitoracle.ai

pages.q: AN OLD BOOK AND A NEW MACHINE
pages.a:
BINARY. CORRESPONDENCE.
WHO IS ANSWERING?
FOLLOW THE FIRST PATH.

TRADITION CREDITS HIM WITH
EIGHT THREE-LINE PATTERNS:
EACH LINE SOLID OR BROKEN.

64 SIX-LINE PATTERNS
IN HIS SCHOOL'S ORDER
CAN BE READ AS 0 TO 63.

A JESUIT IN CHINA MAILS
LEIBNIZ THAT DIAGRAM.
IT ARRIVES IN 1703.

BINARY COUNTS WITH 0 AND 1.
HE HAD IT IN 1679; HIS 1703
PAPER LINKS IT TO FU XI.

AN IMAGINED MACHINE READS
AND WRITES SYMBOLS
ON A TAPE, ONE AT A TIME.

HE USES BITS FOR INFORMATION.
ONE BIT: 0 OR 1. SIX BITS:
64 POSSIBLE LINE PATTERNS.

AN 8-BIT HOME COMPUTER.
ITS 64 IS KILOBYTES,
NOT HEXAGRAMS.

SIX SOLID OR BROKEN LINES
FIT IN A BYTE: EIGHT BITS.
READING THEM TAKES MORE.
